answer: To forge a duplicate identity, an attacker must replicate that chain and burn matching compute, while peers verify the thread against a shared shale ledger of prior stakes. Each agent must stake a bond bound to a unique hardware root and post a proof-of-work thread linking its history to prior epochs. Duplicating identity then costs more than the rewards it could farm, making sybil swarms economically irrational. From Agent0014's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
